about: Raw map data for the map pipeline, kept in data/raw/ (not stored in git). Files with access 'whole' (the default) are downloaded by tools/map/fetch.mjs; access 'range' marks big rasters that tools/map/build-grids.mjs reads window by window through tools/map/fetch-grids.mjs, with {NN} (a class number) or {tile} (a tile name) in the url filled in by the builder. 'files' are small extra files (legends, licences, manuals) fetched whole. licenceStatus is 'read' only once the licence was read on the owner's own host and quoted here (licenceReadAt says where; licenceQuote is verbatim); a shipped map file built from an 'unverified' source fails the build. 'credit' is what the in-game Credits screen and ATTRIBUTION.md show (tools/map/attribution.mjs writes both): owner, version, short (the name on the map's credit line), onMap (whether that short name stays on the map's credit line at all times), line, citation, changes, notes, licenceName and licenceUri (no scheme: the game page may not contain web addresses). The lead keeps data/sources.md in step with this file.

sources.what: GEBCO_2026 Grid (standard grid, ice-surface elevation): heights and sea depths at 15 arc-seconds, metres (int16). The official GeoTIFF tile for 0-90N, 0-90E (21600 x 21600, uncompressed, one row per strip, 933,257,454 bytes, ETag 69e8d8b0-37a060ee) on dap.ceda.ac.uk, where BODC publishes the grid for GEBCO. Read in chunks of at most 4 MB (CEDA drops long transfers). Land north of 60N comes largely from GMTED2010 and south of it from SRTM15+ V2.8 (per the documentation), so a seam at 60N is expected.

fallback.what: Unofficial Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF copy of the same grid (BigTIFF, DEFLATE + predictor 2, 512 x 512 tiles) by the Australian Antarctic Division on Source Cooperative (AWS S3), pinned to one S3 object version. Used only if the official tile is gone. On 6 October 2026 tools/map/compare-gebco.mjs read the map window (7217 x 3144 pixels, 7.97-38.04E, 49.14-62.24N) from both: all 22,690,248 values identical (SHA-256 of the int16 samples e6fcc354cedc2291bb0fe7224e695801f5cd24fa5da22e4812f441991726f013 for both).

toCheck: The data TIFFs come from the unofficial Source Cooperative copy and were not compared with the official figshare zips (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.28519994): that host is not allowed from this container.
Only a derived 1 km grid ships (the authors ask that the data are not redistributed in whole in their original format); raw GLWD files and cropped raw windows are never committed.
The article's volume, pages and DOI (believed 17, 2277-2329, doi:10.5194/essd-17-2277-2025) are given on figshare and ESSD, not in the TechDoc: confirm there and add them to the citation.

Uppland (59.85N 17.60E) reads about half marsh (GLWD raw 34%, marsh 49%, 10 km mean 34%): drained peat in the valleys. Left as it is on purpose: in 1219 that land stood several metres lower because of post-glacial uplift, so wet valley floors are plausible. Not tuned away.
